terminal.description: A shell that starts in the shop's top folder. Run each search and read its list before you save it.

tasks.title: List every drawing
tasks.description:
Hesper's old drawings are `.svg` files, spread over `old-sticks` and the folders inside it, some several levels deep. Save the path of every `.svg` file anywhere in `old-sticks`, one per line, into `drawings.txt` in the top folder.

Check compares the paths in `drawings.txt` with the `.svg` files in `old-sticks`. Each path must lead to its file from the top folder, and the list may be in any order.
nextSteps: Run `find old-sticks` to see how deep the folders go.
Add a test that keeps only names ending in `.svg`.
Read the list: every line ends in `.svg` and starts with `old-sticks`.
Run it again with `>` and the file's name.
hints: `ls` shows one folder at a time. The lesson's command looks in every folder below the one you give it.
`find` takes where to start first, then `-name` and a pattern. Put the pattern in quotes, or the shell changes it first.
Run `find old-sticks -name "*.svg" > drawings.txt` from the top folder.

tasks.title: List every invoice, whatever its capitals
tasks.description:
Idris needs every file in `old-sticks` that has the word invoice anywhere in its name, however it is written: `invoice`, `Invoice` or `INVOICE`. Save their paths, one per line, into `invoices.txt` in the top folder.

Check compares the paths in `invoices.txt` with the names in `old-sticks` that contain invoice in any letter case. The list may be in any order.
nextSteps: Search `old-sticks` for names with invoice in them, and count the lines.
Look at the names in `old-sticks/stick-2/books` with `ls`: not all of them use small letters.
Use the test that ignores letter case, with the word anywhere in the name.
hints: `-name` cares about capitals. The lesson shows a test that does not.
`-iname` matches a pattern in any letter case. A `*` on each side of the word lets it sit anywhere in the name.
Run `find old-sticks -iname "*invoice*" > invoices.txt` from the top folder.

tasks.title: List the proofs folders
tasks.description:
Each client's proofs are in a folder called `proofs`, somewhere in `old-sticks`. Sol also wrote notes called `proofs`, and those are files. Save the path of every folder called `proofs`, and none of the files, one per line, into `proof-folders.txt` in the top folder.

Check compares the paths in `proof-folders.txt` with the folders in `old-sticks` named exactly `proofs`. The list may be in any order.
nextSteps: Search `old-sticks` for the name `proofs` and read what comes back.
Give `ls` one of the paths: a folder lists what it holds, and a file shows only its own name.
Add the test that keeps only folders.
hints: A name can belong to a file or to a folder. The lesson shows a test that tells them apart.
`-type d` keeps only folders. Combine it with `-name`; find prints only what passes both.
Run `find old-sticks -type d -name proofs > proof-folders.txt` from the top folder.
